title: Checks for usage of panic!.
summary: This macro, or panics in general, may be unwanted in production code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of panic! or assertions in a function whose return type is Result.
summary: For some codebases, it is desirable for functions of type result to return an error instead of crashing. Hence panicking macros should be avoided. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Detects C-style underflow/overflow checks.
summary: These checks will, by default, panic in debug builds rather than check whether the operation caused an overflow. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for calls of unwrap[_err]() that will always fail.
summary: If panicking is desired, an explicit panic!() should be used. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks whether some but not all fields of a struct are public.
summary: Most types should either be: Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for manual re-implementations of PartialEq::ne.
summary: PartialEq::ne is required to always return the negated result of PartialEq::eq, which is exactly what the default implementation does. Therefore, there should never be any need to re-implement it. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for binary comparisons to a literal Option::None.
summary: A programmer checking if some foo is None via a comparison foo == None is usually inspired from other programming languages (e.g. foo is None in Python). Checking if a value of type Option<T> is (not) equal to None in that way relies on T: PartialEq to do the comparison, which is unneeded. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Looks for calls to Path::ends_with calls where the argument looks like a file extension.
summary: This doesn’t actually compare file extensions. Rather, ends_with compares the given argument to the last component of the path and checks if it matches exactly. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for calls to push immediately after creating a new PathBuf.
summary: Multiple .join() calls are usually easier to read than multiple .push calls across multiple statements. It might also be possible to use PathBuf::from instead. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for patterns that aren’t exact representations of the types they are applied to.
summary: It increases ownership hints in the code, and will guard against some changes in ownership. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
